Asha — thanks for the note. Attached is a compact MAP (spreadsheet) plus a short markdown with three representative acceptance "vignettes" (small, runnable test cases) we recommend Veridian run during the 4-week evaluation. High-level:

- Goal: Validate production-grade inference for clinical notes summarization and retrieval with 95th percentile latency <= 350ms and F1 concordance >= 0.88 against the gold prompts.
- Exit gates (stoplight):
  * Green: All smoke tests pass + two-week SLA for 95th p99 CPU/GPU utilization within expected band
  * Amber: One major functional test fails but compensating mitigation (reduced throughput + scheduled ops) agreed
  * Red: More than one critical regression in accuracy or a sustained privacy/audit gap -> pause and deep-dive.
- Acceptance tests (owners):
  * Latency & throughput (Redwood / Michael) — load test harness + p95/p99 targets
  * Accuracy / concordance (Veridian / Asha) — pre-defined prompt suite and labeling rubric
  * Security questionnaire follow-ups & evidence (Veridian / Procurement) — SOC2 artifacts, encryption config

Attachments: redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP matrix), eval-test-vignettes.md (3 vignettes and expected pass/fail criteria).

Next steps: If this looks good I suggest we convert the spreadsheet to a shared Drive and lock owners. Kimberly — can you confirm the load test plan and a proposed token budget by EOD? Rishi — can you note fallback model variants (quantized / smaller) we should surface as automatic fallbacks in the MAP?

Looping in our load & reliability note. Quick summary of what I'll run and what counts as pass: 

- Load test plan: 3-day ramp (baseline 10rps -> 150rps sustained), 1-hour p95/p99 sampling windows, spike tests to 300rps for 15m.
- Pass criteria: p95 latency <= 220ms for single-region staged run; p99 <= 350ms. Error rate <= 0.5% across run.
- Observability hooks: token-level cost breakdown, per-route tracing enabled, and KV cache hit-rate metrics. We'll flag if KV hit-rate < 40% — that will trigger an optimization task but not fail the gate by itself.

Attachment: redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated with test owner column). I'll publish the load logs to the shared Drive link.

-Kim

Adding fallback model plan and quick mitigation options:

- Preferred model: redwood-open-7b (quantized inference profile q4_0) — target latency & quality sweet spot.
- Fallbacks: redwood-open-3b (faster, lower cost) and redwood-7b-int8 (if memory/scheduling pressure). Automated routing policy: prefer 7b, if instance queue > 30s use 3b for non-critical batch routes; for critical live inference always surface p95 latency SLA and optionally degrade output if requested by Veridian (opt-in).
- Acceptance impact: any fallback that reduces concordance below 0.82 will be considered a functional regression and requires remediation before move to green.

Proposed timeline (in MAP sheet):
- Week 0 (kickoff): shared Drive MAP live, test owners assigned, security artifacts exchanged.
- Week 1: run smoke scenarios (the three vignettes), baseline load tests.
- Week 2: full run of prompt-suite accuracy tests + user acceptance.
- Week 3: resilience & spike tests, edge-case trace analysis.
- Week 4: handoff meeting and decision vote (go/no-go).

I'll add these variants to the MAP and the routing policies.

-Rishi
